question: A live land, naval or air battle as a save holds it, and everything a load does with it.

addresses.name: CCombatant::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **One side of a battle in a save**, CCombatant slot 2 - held unchanged by the three bombing target combatants, called first by CLandCombatant's and CNavalCombatant's slot 2, and jumped to by CAirCombatant's. In order: `dice` (+0x50, %d); one `unit` `{ id type }` per node of `units` (+0x40), in list order, out of the unit's id pair (CUnit +0x10/+0x14); one `sunk_ship` `{ id type }` per node of `sunk_ships` (+0x28), out of the ship's id pair (CSubUnit +8/+0xC), not out of the node; `losses` (+0x84) as a fixed-point decimal (MakeFixedToken; %d in a binary save); `size` (the vector at +0x74) through SaveWriteFixedVector - one figure per sub-unit definition, the vector never empty; `tactic` - the tactic's own number (CCombatTactic +0x80), %d - **only where the side has a tactic** (+0xAC non-null). Nothing else of the side is written: not is_attacker, countries, own_countries, the destroyed (+0x88) and damage (+0x98) vectors, modifier_used, the byte +0xA8. `ret 4` at 0x56518A. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x565010-0x56518A; token immediates 0x2D2 dice, 0x256 unit, 0x5A1 sunk_ship, 0x2B4 losses, 0x2E size, 0x80F tactic (ghidra/saveTokens.json). Slot 2 of CCombatant and the three target combatants by vtable.py --holding. Every live battle in the maintainer's 33 saves (27 battles, 54 sides) has its side keys in exactly this order; the 48 land sides all have `tactic`, the 6 naval and air sides none. Wrong if a save showed a side key out of this order or a naval side with a tactic.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::SaveContents
addresses.comment: CLandCombatant slot 2: CCombatant::SaveContents, then one `front` `{ id type }` per unit of the front (+0xB0), one `reserves` per unit of the reserves (+0xC0) and one `retreat` per unit of the retreat list (+0xD0), each list in its own order and each key only as the list has nodes. front_set_up (+0xE0) is not written. `ret 4` at 0x569393. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; tokens 0x396 front, 0x398 reserves, 0x1A6 retreat. In the saves: 48 land sides, 46 with a front, 10 with reserves, none with a retreat list, and the two sides with no units carry none of the three; in all 48 the units of front + reserves + retreat are exactly the side's `unit`s. Wrong if a save had a `retreat` before a `front`.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::SaveContents
addresses.comment: CNavalCombatant slot 2: CCombatant::SaveContents, then `positioning` (+0x10B4) as a fixed-point decimal (MakeFixedToken; %d in a binary save). positioning_roll (+0x10B8) and the target list are not written. `ret 4` at 0x568D78. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole. The four naval sides in Ireland1937_07_05_02 and Ireland1937_11_02_21 end in positioning=0.560, 0.730, 1.080, 0.490 - three decimals, so MakeFixedToken and not %d.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::SaveContents
addresses.comment: CAirCombatant slot 2: `push ebp; mov ebp,esp; pop ebp; jmp CCombatant::SaveContents` - an air side writes the base keys and nothing else, never `positioning`, which CAirCombatant::LoadKey accepts and drops. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Five instructions read. Both air sides of Ireland1936_02_02_04's air battle end at `size`.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::AfterLoad
addresses.comment: CLandCombatant slot 5 - the only combatant kind with an AfterLoad of its own; CCombatant's, CNavalCombatant's and CAirCombatant's slot 5 is the empty stub 0xABF890. Clears front_set_up (+0xE0) where the side has units (+0x48 above 0) and its retreat list (+0xD8), reserves (+0xC8) and front (+0xB8) are all empty - a side saved before its battle's first hour. Every CLandCombatant::LoadKey call has set the byte, so a side with any list keeps it. Bare ret. The combat's own AfterLoad (CCombat::AttachAndRegister) then sets up the front of an attacker left clear, and never of a defender. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Nine instructions read, 0x569010-0x569038. vtable.py --holding 0x569010: CLandCombatant slot 5 only; vtable.py --all shows 0xABF890 at slot 5 for the base, naval and air sides. No save of the maintainer's has a land side with units and no list, so the branch that clears was not seen taken.

addresses.name: CMap::FindTerrainByName
addresses.comment: **A terrain by name**: walks the map's terrain vector (CMap +0x2210..+0x2214) from the front and answers the first whose name (the terrain's slot 7) equals `name` byte for byte - a memcmp over the shorter length, then the lengths; null where none does, or where an entry is null. `ret 8`, both arguments on the stack, ECX never read. Four callers: CCombat::LoadKey's `terrain` arm (0x16E11A), and 0xAE92B, 0x1A4D5E, 0x1FF768, not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x491E40-0x491F06; findRefs --callers gives the four. The call site pushes the string then [0x1A8557C] (g_CMap). Wrong if the compare were case-insensitive - 0x415F70 is the plain compare the std::string operators use.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombatManager::LoadKey(CCombatManager* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The keys its switch names**, 7 of them, one case each: `air_combat`, `ground_bombing`, `history`, `land_bombing`, `land_combat`, `naval_bombing`, `naval_combat`. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

**The three battle arms, read 2026-11-05.** `land_combat` (0x2D3), `naval_combat` (0x2D4) and `air_combat` (0x520) each take operator new(0x44) and the kind's constructor (CLandCombat::CLandCombat, CNavalCombat::CNavalCombat, CAirCombat::CAirCombat - day -1, everything else zero), then **CCombatManager::AddCombat, so the battle is on the manager's list before any key of its block is read**, then slot 6 (CreateCombatants: the attacker at +0x10 with is_attacker 1, the defender at +0x14 with 0), then slot 3 (CPersistent::Load) on its block, whose close runs the combat's slot 5 (CCombat::AttachAndRegister). SetProvince is not called: `location` and `terrain` fill those two fields themselves. AddCombat puts a land, naval or air battle at the back of the list, so they come back in the saved order. `history` (0x1E1) is slot 3 on the embedded CCombatHistory (+0x18). The three bombing arms (0x523..0x525) are another reader's. Any other key is dropped with its value unread. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing, 0x42FC60-0x42FE0F: the compare chain on 0x520 / 0x1E1 / 0x2D3 / 0x2D4, and in each arm the order call ctor - call 0x42FFC0 - call [vft+0x18] - call [vft+0xC].

addresses.name: CCombat::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombat::LoadKey(CCombat* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The keys its switch names**, 6 of them, one case each: `attacker`, `day`, `defender`, `duration`, `location`, `terrain`. Inherited by 7 classes in all. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

**Each key, read 2026-11-05.** `location` (0x220): atoi, then **indexed straight into the map's province vector (g_CMap +0x2200) with no bounds check**, into +0x18 - the terrain is not touched. `day` (0x79): atoi into +0x1C. `duration` (0x6C): atoi into +0x20. `terrain` (0x20B): the quoted name looked up with CMap::FindTerrainByName into +0x24, null where no terrain has that name. `attacker` (0x2B1) and `defender` (0x2B2): slot 3 (CPersistent::Load) on the combatant already at +0x10 / +0x14, made by the manager's slot 6 before the block was read - so a second `attacker` block would load into the same side again. Anything else is dropped. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x56E0B0-0x56E200: the arms store to +0x24, +0x1C, +0x20, +0x18 and call [[+0x14]+0xC] / [[+0x10]+0xC]. Wrong if the location arm compared against the vector's end - it does not.

addresses.name: CCombatant::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombatant::LoadKey(CCombatant* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The keys its switch names**, 6 of them, one case each: `dice`, `losses`, `size`, `sunk_ship`, `tactic`, `unit`. Inherited by 4 classes in all. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

**Each key, read 2026-11-05.** `dice` (0x2D2): atoi into +0x50. `unit` (0x256): an `{ id type }` reference (ParseObjectReference into a stack reference, CRef_ResolveAndCache) and, **where it resolves, the side's own slot 12 (AddUnit) with the unit** - so loading a side does what joining it does: the owner onto `countries` and `own_countries`, every brigade's remembered target cleared, the unit's men, ships or wings added into `size`, and on a naval side every ship given a new distance (CNavalCombatant::AddUnit) - but not CUnit::AttachCombat, which waits for the combat's AfterLoad. An id that resolves to nothing is dropped. `losses` (0x2B4): TokenToFixedPoint into +0x84. `size` (0x2E): ReadFixedVectorInPlace into the vector at +0x74, overwriting what the `unit` keys before it added. `tactic` (0x80F): atoi, then CCombatTactics::Get - the tactic of that number, or the null tactic for a number outside the list - into +0xAC. `sunk_ship` (0x5A1): where the value's atoi is 0 (it is a block), an `{ id type }` pair (ParseObjectId) found with FindPersistentByIdPair and, where found, appended to `sunk_ships` (+0x28) - the CShip the top-level `sunk_ships` block made earlier in the file, whose AfterLoad registered it; a non-zero plain number is ignored. Anything else is dropped. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x564DD0-0x565000: compare chain on 0x2D2 / 0x2E / 0x256 / 0x2B4 / 0x5A1 / 0x80F; the unit arm's `call [vft+0x30]` (slot 12) at 0x564E92; the sunk_ships reader in CGameState::LoadKey decompiled (dec2) calls the ship's slot 3, which runs CSubUnit::AfterLoad. Against the saves: the one `sunk_ship` (Ireland1937_11_02_21, id 4775 type 41) is in that save's top-level sunk_ships block.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::LoadKey(CLandCombatant* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **Three keys, not two - corrected 2026-11-05** (definitions.py missed `retreat`, the switch opening with `sub eax, 0x1A6` rather than a compare). It first sets front_set_up (+0xE0) to 1 - on every call, whatever the key, so the first key of any land side sets it. Then `retreat` (0x1A6) appends to the retreat list (+0xD0), `reserves` (0x398) to the reserves (+0xC0), `front` (0x396) to the front (+0xB0): each an `{ id type }` reference resolved as CCombatant::LoadKey's `unit` is, appended **with no duplicate test and without AddUnit**, an unresolved id dropped. Anything else goes to CCombatant::LoadKey. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x569040-0x5692A0: `mov byte [edi+0xE0],1` at 0x56906D before any compare; `sub eax,0x1A6` / `sub eax,0x1F0` / `sub eax,2` give retreat, reserves, front; each arm appends a 0x10-byte node to +0xD0/+0xC0/+0xB0 with no walk of the list first and no call through the vftable. definitions.py's 'front, reserves' is the evidence the old text rested on.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombatant::LoadKey(CNavalCombatant* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The keys its switch names**, 1 of them, one case each: `positioning`. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

`positioning` (0x39B) is read with **ParseFixedPoint** (0x67B540) into +0x10B4 - a fixed-point decimal, `0.560` being 560, **not the %d FINDINGS-combat.md has**; anything else goes to CCombatant::LoadKey. The side's `unit` keys come before it and each runs CNavalCombatant::AddUnit and UpdatePositioning, so this restores the saved figure over theirs. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAirCombatant::LoadKey(CAirCombatant* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The keys its switch names**, 1 of them, one case each: `positioning`. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

`positioning` is matched and dropped with its value unread; CAirCombatant::SaveContents never writes it. Anything else goes to CCombatant::LoadKey. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

addresses.name: CCombat::AttachAndRegister
addresses.comment:
**CCombat virtual slot 5**, and the same implementation in all seven kinds - none of CLandCombat, CNavalCombat, CAirCombat or the three bombings overrides it.

What it does, in order:

1. sets the word at `+0x29` to 1
2. walks the attacker's units (`combat+0x10`, then the combatant's list at `+0x40`, nodes `{ data, ?, next }`) and calls 0x1BFE80 for each
3. the same for the defender at `combat+0x14`
4. asks its own slot 8, and on false appends the combat to its province's combat list through 0xA5F90; on true stores itself at `province+0x2FC` if that is empty
5. goes on to slot 11 (GetKind)

So it is the step that puts a built combat into play: both sides' units attached, and the combat findable from its province. 0xA5F90's other caller is CCombatManager::CreateCombat's tail, which does the same registration - so this is that work reached virtually.

**A known crash site.** It faults at `0x16E391`, reading `defender->units`, when `combat+0x14` holds something that is not a combatant. Seen in a user's dump with `+0x14 == 1`, the attacker a valid combatant and its unit list empty, at **3.62 GB private in a 32-bit address space**.

The obvious reading is CreateCombatants stopping half way: its second `operator new(0xE4)` throws `bad allocation`, so `+0x14` is never written and keeps the combat's own recycled block content, while `+0x10` keeps the attacker it already stored. The unit list is empty because units are added after slot 6, not by it. And the combat is already on the manager's list - CCombatManager::AddCombat runs before slot 6 in both the loader (0x2FCBE) and the live factory (0x31424) - so it stays there for whatever walks that list next to call this and read `0x41`.

**That reading needs a catch above and there is none** - no try block in eight levels of direct callers above CCombatManager::CreateCombat, none in CInGameIdler::Update or DailyUpdate, and one __try in the whole image, in the CRT. An uncaught `bad allocation` ends the process, so it cannot leave a half-built combat for later. The proximate cause is certain and the 3.62 GB is real; the route between them is open. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md.

**It is the combat's AfterLoad and nothing else** (read 2026-11-05): no direct caller and no reference to it in code (findRefs), so it is reached only as slot 5 from CPersistent::Load, as a battle's block closes - after both sides' AfterLoads and after `terrain`. Step 1 writes a **word**: `begun` (+0x29) = 1 and `ended` (+0x2A) = 0, so CCombatManager::Tick never calls Begin (slot 13) for a loaded battle - no battle-started message, no naval positioning roll. Step 2, CUnit::AttachCombat for every unit on each side's `units` list, is the only thing on the load path that gives a unit its list of battles (+0x114) back. The tail the record left as 'goes on to slot 11': **where the kind is 1 (land)**, CLandCombatant::SetUpFrontLine on the attacker where its front_set_up is clear, **then the same test and call on the attacker again** - both read combat +0x10 (0x56E3E6 and 0x56E3F8), where CLandCombat::Begin reads +0x10 and then +0x14 - so a defender's front is never set up here; then CCombat::SumTacticEffects (the combat in EAX), which fills +0x34..+0x40 from the two loaded tactics. Bare ret. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x56E360-0x56E417, set beside CLandCombat::Begin (0x57B6E0), whose two tests read [esi+0x10] and [esi+0x14]. findRefs --callers 0x56E360 and --address 0x56E360: 0 and 0.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::AddUnit
addresses.comment:
CCombatant slot 12 for a naval side: **where every ship is given its distance.** After the base (CCombatant::AddUnit) and CNavalCombatant::UpdatePositioning it counts the unit's ships by type into +0x74 and then sets each ship's current_distance (CSubUnit +0xC8): half the definition's firing_distance, plus a roll of up to `max(300 - spread_out trait, 100) / 1000 * half * (5 - leader skill) * (1 - positioning)` (2 at least); the fleet's first capital ship sets a line, every other ship is put before or behind that line at even odds; a unit joining a battle that has had a round starts 100.000 further out, measured from the side's first capital ship that has a distance; never under 1.000. The 300 is the floor of the float 300.5 (0x1A881A8). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 2. **The leader is the unit's own (+0x12C), with no rank test**, and `5 - skill` is held at nothing (0x566FEC). An admiral of skill 5 or more leaves the roll at its floor of 2, so his ships stand at half their reach **or one further** - not exactly half, as FINDINGS-seabattle.md section 2 says. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 2.

**On a load it runs once for every `unit` key of a naval side** (CCombatant::LoadKey), after the battle's `day` has been read: where the battle had had a round, every ship is placed as a late joiner - half its firing distance plus a fresh roll, **plus 100.000**, a capital ship from nothing and any other ship either side of the first capital ship's distance as the save left it - and the `current_distance` each ship carried in the save is overwritten. Every draw is the game's generator. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The function's own body (decompiled, dec1) with CCombatant::LoadKey's unit arm calling slot 12, and CCombat::SaveContents writing `day` before `attacker`. Not seen in a running game.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::AddUnit
addresses.comment:
CLandCombatant slot 12: CCombatant::AddUnit, then each brigade's men added to the side's count by type (+0x74: strength * slot 14 / 1000), and - where the front has been set up (+0xE0) and a game is on screen - the unit appended to the reserves (+0xC0) unless it is there. **A unit that joins late starts in reserve.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 1.

On a load (CCombatant::LoadKey's `unit`) front_set_up is already set but `in_game` is clear - a save is loaded in the lobby (FINDINGS-session.md) - so no unit goes to the reserves here; the saved `front`, `reserves` and `retreat` lists are the whole placement. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The in_game test at 0x5694AE (`cmp byte [esi+0xDA4],0`) on the game state; in_game's writers per FINDINGS-session.md section 1.

addresses.name: CUnit::ShowFighting
addresses.comment:
Zeroes CUnit +0xA8 and +0xAC, and is otherwise the avatar: the `attack` animation, facing the next province, the province's fighting point, the arrow. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 1.

+0xA8 and +0xAC are `disengage` and `disengage_to` (saved as `disengage` and `possible_retreat`; CUnit::SaveContents reads them at this-0x8 = +0xA0/+0xA4). **CInGameIdler::Enter calls it for every unit whose combats count (+0x11C) is above 0, with CUnit::IsAttackerHere (0x65BAD8-0x65BAEE, both kinds of game)** - so in a loaded game every unit of every loaded battle has its disengage count and its destination from the save zeroed before the first hour. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: `mov [ebx+0xA8],edi; mov [ebx+0xAC],edi` with edi = 0 at 0x5C7991-0x5C7999, unconditional; Enter's call site read on the listing, reached from both arms at 0x65B8ED and the fall-through. Wrong if CUnit::SaveContents's 0x507/0x508 read other fields - they read [ebx+0xA0]/[ebx+0xA4] with ebx = the unit's CPersistent at +8.

struct_fields.name: province
struct_fields.comment: province fought over Loaded from `location` (the province id) by indexing the map's province vector with no bounds check; CCombat::LoadKey does not call SetProvince, so the terrain comes only from `terrain`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: duration
struct_fields.comment: saved as `duration`, the key CCombat::SaveContents writes it under **Read 2026-11-05: the hours begun.** CCombat::Tick adds one at its start, before anything else of the hour but StampWars and the tactic pick, which tests `duration % (TACTIC_SWAP_FREQUENCEY/1000)` with the value before the increment; HasLost is asked only once it is 4 or more, an air battle ends at 4, a naval one may break off from its third hour and CNavalCombat::MayLeave lets a fleet go above 3. `day` (+0x1C) is -1 until the first round sets it to 0 and gains one at the end of every hour that does not end the battle, so after any whole hour the two are equal - as in all 27 battles in the saves - and they differ (day -1, duration 0) only before the first hour. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: CCombat::Tick: `inc [esi+0x20]` at 0x56EC53 unconditionally, `mov [esi+0x1C],0` at 0x56F0B6 in the day == -1 branch, `inc [esi+0x1C]` at 0x56F351 on the not-over exit only, `cmp [esi+0x20],4` at 0x56F1E8.

struct_fields.name: terrain
struct_fields.comment: terrain, unverified Saved as `terrain` by its name (the terrain's slot 7) only where set, and loaded by name through CMap::FindTerrainByName - null where no terrain of the map has that name; in play SetProvince sets it from the province. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: begun
struct_fields.comment: Clear until the combat is in play: CCombatManager::Tick calls slot 13 (Begin) before the round while it is. CCombat::AttachAndRegister sets it after a load. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 3. CCombat::AttachAndRegister writes the word at +0x29, so a load also leaves `ended` (+0x2A) at 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: dice
struct_fields.comment: saved as `dice`: this side's roll **Read 2026-11-05:** CCombat::Tick sets it every hour to Random() % 10, the attacker's before the defender's (the first hour rolls the pair twice), so the saved figure is the last hour's roll and the next hour replaces it before the side shoots. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: own_countries
struct_fields.comment: this side's own countries, kept when the list above is emptied Not saved: a load rebuilds it, like `countries`, from the owners of the units the `unit` keys add, so a country whose units had all left the side before the save is no longer on it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: CCombatant::AddUnit appends to both lists; CCombatant::RemoveUnit rebuilds only +0x54. What reads +0x64 was not looked for.

struct_fields.name: men_begin
struct_fields.comment: men per subunit type in thousandths, begin **Saved as `size`, read 2026-11-05.** Indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index: entry 0 is the database's null definition `---`, then one entry per unit type in the order the sub-unit loader read them - the `units/*.txt` files in byte order of their file names (an upper-case name before any lower-case one), a type's index being its file's place plus one; 58 in Their Finest Hour, which has 57 unit files. A side's AddUnit adds to it as each unit joins: on land the brigade's strength x MenPerStrength / 1000, at sea and in the air 1000 a ship or wing; nothing in the combat module takes from it, so it is everything that ever joined the side, counted at joining. CCombat::Conclude sums it / 1000 for the battle's message. Written whole by SaveWriteFixedVector; read in place by ReadFixedVectorInPlace after the `unit` keys, so the saved figures replace what those added. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Indices against the saves: bergsjaeger_brigade 14, battlecruiser 12, destroyer 19, light_cruiser 32, interceptor 29, submarine 50, tactical_bomber 53 - each the file's place in byte order plus one, checked on the units of Ireland1936_02_02_04, Ireland1937_07_05_02 and Ireland1937_11_02_21; the loader's decompilation (dec1) pushes the null definition first and constructs each later one with a counter starting at 1. A chunk sweep of 0x560000-0x580000 for indexed uses of [x+0x74] finds only adds.

struct_fields.name: losses
struct_fields.comment: strength lost in thousandths Saved as `losses`, a fixed-point decimal, and read back with TokenToFixedPoint. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: tactic
struct_fields.comment: The combat tactic in use, or null. Saved as `tactic` out of its number (+0x80), which the loader looks back up. Written by CCombatant::PickTactic. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 11. The number is the tactic's place in `common/combat_tactics.txt`, counting from 1 (tactic_basic_attack 1, tactic_basic_defend 2 ... in Their Finest Hour); written only where a tactic is held, which in the saves is every land side and no other. A number outside the list loads as the null tactic, which counts as held, so the side is not given a new one until the swap hour. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: CCombatant::SaveContents 0x565139-0x56517F; CCombatTactics::Get 0x43A2F0 (0 <= n < count, else 0x1A85550). Attackers' saved tactics 1, 3, 4, 8 and defenders' 2, 6, 9, 13 are attack and defence tactics in that order.

struct_fields.name: positioning
struct_fields.comment: Naval positioning, thousandths, save key `positioning` (0x39B). Rolled once at combat start by CNavalCombat slot 13 (0x17B910) and then written by CNavalCombatant::UpdatePositioning (0x166E70) as `clamp0(+0x10B8 + 400 + leaderSkill*100 - stackPenalty)`; CNavalCombatant::Attack (slot 15) adds 20 a tick while it is below `max(100, 400 + leaderSkill*100 - stackPenalty)`. leaderSkill is CLeader.skill (+0x70) of the highest-ranked real leader on the side; stackPenalty is NavalStackingPositionPenalty (0x1D5B80). **The base 400, the per-tick 20 and the skill weight 100 are all hardcoded literals, not defines** - only the three NAVAL_STACK_POS_* defines are mod-facing. Because the die can be up to 190, a side can start above its own cap and then never move. What positioning is multiplied into is not established. Saved and loaded as a fixed-point decimal (MakeFixedToken / ParseFixedPoint), after the side's `unit` keys have recomputed it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: positioning_roll
struct_fields.comment: The positioning die: `(rand() % 20) * 10`, i.e. 0..190 thousandths, rolled once per side by CNavalCombat slot 13 (0x17B978 for the attacker, 0x17B9D8 for the defender) and added straight into +0x10B4 by UpdatePositioning. Never re-rolled. FINDINGS-combat.md records it as zeroed beside +0x10B4 with nothing known about it. Not saved: zero after a load, and since a loaded battle never runs CNavalCombat::RollPositioning again, a fleet that joins it later has its side's positioning recomputed by UpdatePositioning without the roll. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Absent from CNavalCombatant::SaveContents; AttachAndRegister sets begun.

struct_fields.name: retreat
struct_fields.comment: Saved as `retreat`. CLandCombatant::UpdateFrontLine moves a unit here that can fight to the reserves and CLandCombatant::IsSpent averages over it with the front; nothing read puts a unit on it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 2. **Loaded as well as saved**, by CLandCombatant::LoadKey (corrected 2026-11-05). No save of the maintainer's has one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: CLandCombatant::LoadKey's 0x1A6 arm; the 48 land sides in the saves.

struct_fields.name: front_set_up
struct_fields.comment: Set by CLandCombatant::SetUpFrontLine and by LoadKey. Clear, CLandCombat::Begin sets the front up; set, a unit that joins goes to the reserves. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 2. **On a load**: set by the first key of the side's block; cleared by CLandCombatant::AfterLoad where the side has units on none of its three lists; then CCombat::AttachAndRegister sets up the attacker's front where it is clear, and never the defender's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: The three functions' records, all read 2026-11-05.

struct_fields.name: current_distance
struct_fields.comment: how far the regiment is from the enemy in its battle, x1000, saved as `current_distance` - and only where the unit's `combats` list has something in it. **Read live**: zero on all 4000 regiments **For a ship it does not survive a load**: CNavalCombatant::AddUnit, run for each `unit` of a naval side, rolls every ship's distance again - 100.000 further out where the battle had had a round. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savedbattle.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: CNavalCombatant::AddUnit's store at its end, reached from CCombatant::LoadKey's unit arm.
